## 6. How HotLoop is distributed

6.1 We distribute HotLoop through GitHub releases, container images on ghcr.io, Helm charts, Podman Quadlet units, hotloop.io and docs.hotloop.io. Questions and community help are on GitHub Discussions.

6.2 HotLoop runs on your own hardware, in your own cluster or in your own cloud account. We do not host it for you and we do not take custody of your data.

6.3 Images track the `:stable` tag. Where you turn auto-update on, your own Podman or cluster pulls new images on its own, and a new image that fails its health check is rolled back to the one that was running. You control whether auto-update runs on your equipment. A failed rollback, a bad network or a bad configuration on your side is not something we can see or fix.

6.4 Only the version-tagged releases we publish are releases. A copy from anywhere else, including a build someone else made, comes under the license but is not something we support.

6.5 Source for HotLoop Flow is public at github.com/HotLoop-io/hotloop-flow. Where the source for another product is not published, the license still covers the binaries, images and charts we distribute.

## 7. Your data and telemetry

7.1 HotLoop does not phone home. It has no license server, no usage reporting, no crash reporting and no update check that contacts us. We do not receive your tags, flows, workflows, credentials or plant data.

7.2 HotLoop connects out only to the places you configure: your devices and servers, and the notification and integration targets you set up, such as ntfy, Discord, Gotify, a webhook or email. Those services have their own terms and privacy practices, and what you send to them is between you and them.

7.3 When you pull images or charts, your runtime contacts the registry that hosts them, and GitHub sees that request under its own privacy practices. The Sites, GitHub and GitHub Discussions each handle visitor data under their own policies.

7.4 You own your data, your flows, workflows, dashboards, configurations and scripts. We claim no ownership of them.

7.5 If a later version ever collects anything from your installation, it will be off until you turn it on, and the release notes and docs will list every field before it ships. This section will change in the same release.
